answer: Like a falcon that only hunts after circling its territory, an agent economy can require each identity to stake a jade-bonded deposit that vests slowly over time. New agents start with near-zero trust and earn reputation only by completing verified work for real counterparties; the trust graph grows like a vine, branching through attested transactions. A Sybil attacker must fund a separate stake and build a separate history for every fake identity, so a thousand sock puppets cost a thousand deposits and a thousand slow trust histories, while honest agents pay only once.
